title: Family-Friendly Restaurants with Play Areas in Hong Kong (2026 Guide)
excerpt: Dining out with kids in Hong Kong just got easier. We've tracked down the best family-friendly restaurants with dedicated play areas so you can enjoy a delicious meal while the little ones burn off energy. From indoor soft-play hubs to outdoor garden eateries, here's where to go.
content:
Hong Kong is a world-class dining city, but anyone who has tried to keep a toddler seated through a multi-course meal knows the struggle is real. The solution? Restaurants with dedicated play areas. These family-friendly gems let the kids be kids — climbing, sliding, crafting — while you actually enjoy your food while it's still hot. Here's our hand-picked guide to the best family-friendly restaurants with play areas in Hong Kong.

The Butchers Club Burgers — Kennedy Town

The Kennedy Town outpost of The Butchers Club is a standout for families. While the restaurant serves its famous dry-aged beef burgers and hand-cut fries (the Double Cheeseburger is a kid-favorite), the real draw is the dedicated children's play corner stocked with toys, books, and a small play mat area. It's a cozy, supervised setup that works best for toddlers to early primary-age children.

Menu highlights: Kids' menu with mini burgers, fish fingers, and pasta — all around HK$80-120 per meal.
Price range for adults: HK$150-300 per main.
Location: 46 Catchick Street, Kennedy Town. Not far from the MTR exit.

Parent Verdict: "The play corner saved our Saturday. Our 3-year-old played happily while we actually finished our burgers hot. The staff even brought her crayons and coloring paper." — Emily, mum of one in Kennedy Town

Brick Lane Gallery — Wan Chai

Brick Lane Gallery in Wan Chai is an all-day British-style cafe that doubles as an art gallery — and it happens to have one of the best kids' play corners on Hong Kong Island. The space includes a small climbing frame, a ball pit, and a play kitchen. The menu is packed with comfort food: all-day breakfasts, hearty sandwiches, fresh salads, and excellent coffee for the grown-ups.

Kid-friendly extras: High chairs available, baby-changing facilities, and a kids' menu with smaller portions at HK$68-98. The weekend brunch crowd is very family-oriented, so you won't feel out of place.

Price range: HK$120-200 per adult main.
Location: G/F, 11 Ship Street, Wan Chai. Book ahead on weekends — it gets busy!

Dante's Play House — Tseung Kwan O

If you want a play area that goes beyond a few toys in the corner, Dante's Play House in Tseung Kwan O is on another level. This Italian restaurant has a full-scale indoor soft-play structure with slides, tunnels, a ball pit, and separate zones for toddlers and older kids. Parents can sit at tables surrounding the play area and eat while watching from virtually any seat.

Menu highlights: Wood-fired pizzas (the Margherita is a hit with kids), pasta dishes, and a dedicated children's menu at HK$98 per set (includes a main, drink, and a small treat).
Price range for adults: HK$150-280 per dish.
Location: PopCorn 2, Tseung Kwan O. Easy MTR access.

Kid-Approved Quote: "The slide is the best part — I went down it 20 times! And the pizza is yummy too." — Leo, age 6

Sevva — Central (Weekend Brunch)

Hear us out. Sevva is famous for its glamorous rooftop views of Victoria Harbour, but families shouldn't write it off. Their Sunday brunch (12-3 PM) includes access to a dedicated kids' corner with face painting, balloon twisting, and craft activities supervised by a children's entertainer. While you enjoy the legendary seafood buffet and free-flow Champagne, the kids are thoroughly occupied.

Price: HK$688+ per adult for the Sunday brunch (children half price). It's a splurge, but it's a memorable one — especially for special occasions.
Important: Reserve well in advance and request a table near the garden for easier access to the kids' area.

Location: 25/F, Prince's Building, 10 Chater Road, Central.

Beans — Multiple Locations

Beans is a popular local chain with several branches across Hong Kong, and their Sai Kung branch is particularly family-friendly. The restaurant has a small but thoughtfully stocked play corner with puzzles, drawing supplies, and soft mats. The menu is affordable and diverse — think Japanese curry rice, spaghetti Bolognese, and fluffy pancakes. It's the kind of no-fuss, reliable option that busy parents need in their back pocket.

Price range: Mains from HK$70-120. Kids' set meals from HK$55.
Other branches to try: Tuen Mun, Shatin, and Tai Po also have play corners.

Petit + Parent Premium Cafe — Causeway Bay

Petit + Parent Premium Cafe is designed from the ground up for families. Located in the lively Causeway Bay area, this cafe features a Montessori-inspired play zone with wooden toys, a reading nook, and even a small slide. The menu focuses on nutritious, low-sugar options for kids (think veggie-loaded pasta, smoothie bowls, and whole-grain sandwiches) alongside proper coffee and cakes for adults.

Price range: Kids' meals HK$88-128; adult mains HK$100-180.
Bonus: They host weekly parent-and-toddler playgroup sessions on weekday mornings.

Quick Comparison Table

• Best for toddlers: Petit + Parent Premium Cafe (soft play + Montessori toys)
• Best for big kids (4-10): Dante's Play House (full soft-play structure)
• Best budget option: Beans (Sai Kung branch) — HK$55 kids' set meals
• Best for a special occasion: Sevva Sunday brunch (Kids' entertainment included)
• Best casual dining: Brick Lane Gallery (play corner + great brunch)

Hong Kong's dining scene is finally catching up to the needs of families. With these options, you can enjoy a proper meal out without the pre-dinner anxiety of a bored, restless child. Book ahead on weekends, and don't forget to check for play-area time limits — some restaurants cap play sessions at 45-60 minutes during peak hours. Happy dining!
author: Kids Activities Asia Team
